title: Supplied uniformizer root normalization at general ordinary coefficients
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite intermediate extension, pi in O_E, n natural, and A any ordinary commutative ring killed by l^(n+1). Let X be a scheme and e a FiniteRealization from the condensed actual quotient ring O_E/(pi)^(n+1) to ordinary A-modules [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-finite-realization]. UniformizerRootFrame records an IntegralRoots, kernel-normalized FiniteRoots, and an e.LineEndpoint between the ordinary quotient of the integral Tate line and geoCartierLine(A,l^(n+1),hA,X), normalized by the n-th integral-root projection [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-quotient-line]. There is no class equation or existence claim. At A=ULift(completedResidue l E pi n), its three fields are exactly the three supplied sigma components of QuotientLineRealization. UniformizerSquareData groups this root frame, a CoefficientArrowRoute, the two finite realizations, FiniteSourceComparison, a CyclicCartierFrame [def-diagonal-cyclic-cartier-frame] and CartierScalarMaps [def-diagonal-coefficient-arrow-transport]. Its irreducible equation definition names exactly the coefficient Yoneda square: mk0 of the supported source map composed with restriction of the realized quotient class equals the realized cyclic class composed with mk0 of the line map. No Cartier class equality is a field, and the equation is a definition of a proposition rather than an assertion of it. Leaving A as a parameter and storing the supplied data in a structure lets statements share these types rather than repeat their concrete ring instances and endpoint expressions.
